Build a triangle BVH over the coarse mesh by inserting four triangular faces facing outside for every coarse element.
Trace rays into the BVH using OptiX Wrapper Library (OWL) hit and miss functions.
The hit function returns the hit point and the coarse tetrahedron ID.
The miss function reports no intersection with BVH faces.
**Time Complexity:** $O(\log N)$ for balanced trees, where $N$ is the number of voxels, assuming uniform distribution.
In sparse scenes, it approaches $O(1)$ for empty regions.
**Strengths:** Efficient skipping of empty space; reduced number of intersection tests; suitable for sparse data.
**Limitations:** Overhead of tree traversal; potential for stack overflow in deep trees; complexity of implementation compared to flat grid traversal.
